From 291d044fd51f8484066300ee42afecf8c8db7b3a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Shung-Hsi Yu <shung-hsi.yu@suse.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2023 13:39:03 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Fix precision tracking for BPF_ALU | BPF_TO_BE | BPF_END
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

BPF_END and BPF_NEG has a different specification for the source bit in
the opcode compared to other ALU/ALU64 instructions, and is either
reserved or use to specify the byte swap endianness. In both cases the
source bit does not encode source operand location, and src_reg is a
reserved field.

backtrack_insn() currently does not differentiate BPF_END and BPF_NEG
from other ALU/ALU64 instructions, which leads to r0 being incorrectly
marked as precise when processing BPF_ALU | BPF_TO_BE | BPF_END
instructions. This commit teaches backtrack_insn() to correctly mark
precision for such case.

While precise tracking of BPF_NEG and other BPF_END instructions are
correct and does not need fixing, this commit opt to process all BPF_NEG
and BPF_END instructions within the same if-clause to better align with
current convention used in the verifier (e.g. check_alu_op).

Fixes: b5dc0163d8fd ("bpf: precise scalar_value tracking")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Mohamed Mahmoud <mmahmoud@redhat.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/r/87jzrrwptf.fsf@toke.dk
Tested-by: Toke Høiland-Jørgensen <toke@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Tao Lyu <tao.lyu@epfl.ch>
Acked-by: Eduard Zingerman <eddyz87@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Shung-Hsi Yu <shung-hsi.yu@suse.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231102053913.12004-2-shung-hsi.yu@suse.com
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

diff --git a/kernel/bpf/verifier.c b/kernel/bpf/verifier.c
index def99b1a2b17..bd1c42eb540f 100644
--- a/kernel/bpf/verifier.c
+++ b/kernel/bpf/verifier.c
@@ -3742,7 +3742,12 @@ static int backtrack_insn(struct bpf_verifier_env *env, int idx, int subseq_idx,
 	if (class == BPF_ALU || class == BPF_ALU64) {
 		if (!bt_is_reg_set(bt, dreg))
 			return 0;
-		if (opcode == BPF_MOV) {
+		if (opcode == BPF_END || opcode == BPF_NEG) {
+			/* sreg is reserved and unused
+			 * dreg still need precision before this insn
+			 */
+			return 0;
+		} else if (opcode == BPF_MOV) {
 			if (BPF_SRC(insn->code) == BPF_X) {
 				/* dreg = sreg or dreg = (s8, s16, s32)sreg
 				 * dreg needs precision after this insn
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/bpf/verifier.c`**
- The `backtrack_insn` function was modified to handle the `BPF_END` and `BPF_NEG` opcodes differently from other ALU/ALU64 instructions.
- A new conditional check was added to return early if the opcode is `BPF_END` or `BPF_NEG`, indicating that the source register (`sreg`) is reserved and unused, while the destination register (`dreg`) still requires precision tracking.
- The existing check for the `BPF_MOV` opcode was moved into an `else if` clause to maintain clarity and ensure that the new checks for `BPF_END` and `BPF_NEG` are processed first.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The changes made to the `backtrack_insn` function are aimed at improving the precision tracking mechanism for specific BPF instructions (`BPF_END` and `BPF_NEG`). By distinguishing these opcodes from other ALU operations, the patch ensures that the precision of the destination register is correctly maintained, thereby preventing incorrect marking of the register as precise.
- The modification aligns with the existing conventions in the verifier, as it groups the handling of `BPF_END` and `BPF_NEG` together, similar to how other operations are processed, which enhances code readability and maintainability.

```c
if (class == BPF_ALU || class == BPF_ALU64) {
    if (opcode == BPF_MOV) {
```
Reason:
The `backtrack_insn()` function does not differentiate between `BPF_END` and `BPF_NEG` instructions and other ALU/ALU64 instructions. This oversight causes the destination register (`r0`) to be incorrectly marked as precise when processing `BPF_ALU | BPF_TO_BE | BPF_END` instructions, despite the fact that the source bit in these opcodes is reserved and does not encode the source operand location.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (opcode == BPF_END || opcode == BPF_NEG) {
    /* sreg is reserved and unused
     * dreg still need precision before this insn
     */
    return 0;
```
Reason:
The patch modifies the `backtrack_insn()` function to correctly handle `BPF_END` and `BPF_NEG` instructions by adding a specific check for these opcodes. This ensures that the source register (`sreg`) is treated as reserved and unused, preventing the incorrect marking of the destination register (`dreg`) as precise, thus aligning the behavior with the specifications of these instructions.
